visual_text: Cranberry and urine infections: it depends who was studied
People with a urine infection, out of 100, during the trials
Women who keep getting urine infections: 24 in 100 without cranberry, 18 in 100 with it. Probably fewer infections (moderate certainty).
Older people in care homes or other institutions: about 11 in 100 either way. No clear benefit shown. Uncertain: anything from about 4 fewer to about 3 more per 100.
Williams et al., Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, 2023
alt_text: Bar chart of urine infections per 100 people during trials. Women with repeat infections: 24 without cranberry, 18 with it (probably fewer, moderate certainty).
